newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ships ready for possible Cambodia evacuation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ships ready for possible Cambodia evacuation.

text.p: The United States has put three ships carrying marines and helicopters on alert in Japan in case it is decided to evacuate U.S. citizens from Cambodia, a Pentagon spokesman said on Tuesday.
Spokeswoman Lt. Com. Karen Jeffries said the three ships in an amphibious group based at Sasebo in Japan were ordered on alert by the commander-in-chief of the Pacific Command in Hawaii.

She said the Belleau Wood, the Fort McHenry and the Dubuque, each of which carries several hundred marines and helicopters, were engaged in "contingency planning for their potential use (for) evacuating non-combatants and maybe third country nationals" from Cambodia.

She said she did not know whether any of the ships, which had been due to begin an exercise in a few days, had actually left Sasebo. It would take them about four days to reach the Cambodian coast, she said.

Another U.S. official who asked not to be identified said it appeared the situation was actually easing in Cambodia after days of ferocious fighting between rival factions in the capital Phnom Penh, making an evacuation less likely.
"The Pentagon is preparing for possible contingency if something were to be necessary but so far the situation is becoming more calm (rather) than less calm," he said.
"I think this is prudent preparation for a possible future need but not something that's acually going on right now," he added.

Earlier on Tuesday eight flights of Thai Air Force C-130s brought 800 people, mainly Thais but some foreigners, from the Cambodian capital after three days of violence that claimed at least 58 lives. More planes were due to fly out later Tuesday.
The Phnom Penh fighting began on Saturday after troops loyal to co-Premier Hun Sen moved against those supporting First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
